chemistry_scientist.state_summary: Round 3 contains 429 observed records, 2901 eligible candidates, no pending records, and no validation or test records. The latest feedback revises the nitrogen and hydroxyl hypotheses substantially. Large nitrogen corrections learned from quinoline and pyridyl ketone data failed to transfer to pyridyl ester m90 and phenylpyridine m211, whereas aminoacetophenone m36 was much later than predicted. Hydroxyl-plus-ester and hydroxyl-plus-ether responses remain strongly graph dependent. The objective is overall Row V1/V2 accuracy after retraining; adaptive residuals do not estimate that accuracy.

important_observations.observation: Nitrogen transfer is now clearly topology specific. m90 measured 10.18/20.93 mL at 1/1 and 27.48/65.41 at 5/1, versus current predictions of 8.46/27.83 and 46.45/106.71. m211 measured 11.61/19.38 at 5/1 and 18.13/30.88 at 10/1, versus 20.42/34.37 and 36.26/60.31. These results reject the predicted steep pyridyl-ester and phenylpyridine responses. m66 in pure EA measured 5.57/21.09 versus 6.48/14.28 predicted, so even within pyridyl carbonyl chemistry the endpoint response is not a simple extension of the 2/1 and 5/1 late-retention records.

The amino-ketone environment behaves differently from the ring-N examples. m36 measured 11.68/21.33 at 1/1 and 23.42/39.43 at 2/1, while predictions were 6.25/17.24 and 7.43/22.48. This supports connectivity-specific nitrogen behavior, but it does not support a uniform nitrogen correction.

Hydroxyl response errors remain large and molecule dependent. m99 measured 38.99/58.03 at 10/1 after 19.91/32.37 at 5/1, while its 10/1 prediction was 18.40/29.34. Methoxybenzyl alcohol m120 measured 19.89/29.02 at 2/1 and 50.73/71.53 at 5/1, versus 11.63/21.60 and 18.63/38.05 predicted. m61 at 2/1 measured 12.34/21.99, above its prediction and distinct from m60 at 2/1 (10.43/16.98). Hydroxyl count alone is insufficient.

Beta-ketoester interpolation and molecular transfer separate. m82 at 5/1 was predicted accurately at 12.32/29.34, but related m94 at 20/1 measured 37.25/79.67 versus 29.19/65.10 predicted. The acquired m82 curve improves local interpolation without establishing transfer to every beta-ketoester graph.

The m194 broad completion interval did not persist at half loading. At 117.7 mg, m194 measured 4.35/36.18 at 1/1 and 8.20/26.57 at 5/1. At 58.85 mg it measured 4.26/10.34 at 1/1 and 5.93/14.73 at 2/1. This supports loading-dependent completion broadening or another loading-conditioned effect, while rejecting persistence of the high-loading interval under the tested lower loading.

m173 continues to show a localized ratio and plug dependence. At 1/1, the 1500 uL plug measured 6.04/78.37 versus 6.51/108.89 with 2000 uL; at 2/1 the corresponding completions were 46.22 and 45.06. The 1500 uL experiment at 5/1 measured 11.88/61.87, and pure EA measured 3.56/31.91. These records do not establish a causal plug mechanism, but they argue against a universal solvent monotonicity correction.

The naphthyl shape hypothesis is weakened further. m124 at 20/1 measured 6.31/13.08, rejecting its predicted 19.30/19.54 delayed-onset, compressed-interval response. m40 at 20/1 did rise to 20.33/37.51, but the predicted onset of 26.08 was too late while completion was close. Response shape therefore remains graph specific within the naphthyl family.

Ordinary Row chemistry remains useful for calibration. m176 measured 4.43/14.45 at 5/1 and 4.73/18.69 at 20/1, so its predicted weak-eluent onset increase was excessive. m63 measured 5.91/13.93 at 5/1 and 9.96/25.76 at 20/1, opposing the predicted earlier onset at 20/1. m121 was close at 10/1, and m21 was close at 2/1; at 5/1 its measured onset was later and completion earlier than predicted.

In normal-phase silica chromatography, increasing EA generally strengthens elution. Basic or accessible nitrogen, hydroxyl, sulfoxide and carbonyl groups can increase silica interaction through hydrogen bonding or acid-base effects. Steric accessibility, conjugation, intramolecular hydrogen bonding, dissolution and loading-solvent effects can modify these trends. These are chemical priors, not findings about any particular unmeasured candidate.

possible_model_blind_spots: Graph similarity and shared HBA/HBD or TPSA descriptors appear to transfer large solvent corrections across incompatible nitrogen topologies. The m90 and m211 results show that retention level and solvent slope need separate graph-conditioned learning.

The model can underpredict both endpoints for hydroxylated graphs while overpredicting completion for other oxygenated graphs. A single polarity correction would mix m99, m120, m194 and m173 error structures.

Loading features remain weakly expressed in current predictions despite measured endpoint-specific effects, especially m194 completion broadening and earlier m92 condition contrasts. The packet does not identify whether the cause is feature scaling, condition encoding, graph-condition interaction capacity or record variation.
Sparse ratio coverage encourages implausible extrapolation and nonmonotone predictions. The measured m66, m99 and m173 curves show that a smooth universal solvent law is unsafe.

Candidate quantile ordering defects remain present, including crossed or negative apparent widths. Quantile width is therefore not calibrated uncertainty and should not be used as a stand-alone information-value signal.

Repeated catalog IDs can encode the same full physical input. Such multiplicity is relevant to Row representativeness but usually adds little new chemical information unless replication addresses a defined ambiguity.

The m73 pair, m173 plug comparisons, m194 loading comparison and other unusual records should be preserved as conflicting or conditional evidence. None alone establishes a universal chromatographic mechanism.

ml_scientist.state_summary: Seed 6101, round 3 has 429 observed records, 2901 eligible candidates, no pending records, and no validation or test truth. Recent measured feedback rejects several prior continuation hypotheses: the transferred steep nitrogen response was too large for m90 and m211, the predicted m36 retention was too low, hydroxyl response growth was again underpredicted, m124 did not show the predicted delayed onset, and the broad m194 interval did not persist at lower loading. The remaining learning problem is graph-by-condition and endpoint-specific.
important_observations: Observed measured evidence: m90 at 5/1 measured 27.48/65.41 mL versus 46.45/106.71 predicted. m211 measured 11.61/19.38 at 5/1 and 18.13/30.88 at 10/1 versus 20.42/34.37 and 36.26/60.31 predicted. This weakens the prior transfer of quinoline and pyridyl-ketone corrections to pyridyl ester and phenylpyridine graphs.

Observed measured evidence: m36 measured 11.68/21.33 at 1/1 and 23.42/39.43 at 2/1, versus 6.25/17.24 and 7.43/22.48 predicted. m66 in pure EA also retained a completion underprediction, 5.58/21.09 versus 6.48/14.28. Nitrogen errors therefore remain connectivity-specific and can change sign across graphs.

Observed measured evidence: m99 at 10/1 measured 38.99/58.03 versus 18.40/29.34 predicted; m120 measured 19.89/29.02 at 2/1 and 50.73/71.53 at 5/1 versus 11.63/21.60 and 18.63/38.05 predicted; m61 at 2/1 exceeded prediction by 5.19/9.12 mL. The hydroxyl hypothesis is strengthened, while a common hydroxyl correction remains inadequate.

Observed measured evidence: m82 interpolation at 5/1 was close, but m94 at 20/1 still measured 37.25/79.67 versus 29.19/65.10 predicted. Beta-ketoester response transfer is partial, with completion extrapolation still weak.

Observed measured evidence: m194 high-load 1/1 was 4.35/36.18, while lower-load 1/1 and 2/1 were 4.26/10.34 and 5.93/14.73. The broad interval is not loading-independent; this weakens the previous m194 persistence hypothesis.

Observed measured evidence: m173 at 5/1 with the smaller plug was 11.88/61.87 and close to prediction; pure EA at the same plug was 3.56/31.91, while the 1/1 smaller-plug record remained late at 78.37 completion. The unusual tail is localized near 1/1, with a possible ratio-by-plug interaction still unresolved.

Observed measured evidence: m124 at 20/1 measured 6.31/13.07 versus 19.30/19.54 predicted. This weakens the proposed cross-functionality naphthyl onset delay and interval compression. m40 also had an overly late predicted onset, although its completion was closer.

Observed measured evidence: m80's intermediate completion maximum remains rejected at tested ratios; further extensive m80 weak-eluent sampling has low marginal value. The conflicting m73 1/1 records continue to weaken transfer of its original anomaly.

possible_model_blind_spots: ML diagnostic and inference: loading amount, loading solvent, plug volume, and their interactions with graph structure remain weakly expressed. This is suggested by nearly flat predictions at measured m92 loading contrasts, not by held-out accuracy.

Endpoint residuals are heterogeneous. m36 and m120 show joint retention underprediction, m194 mainly exposes completion behavior, and m91 exposes interval-shape error. A single endpoint offset would mix distinct failure modes.
Sparse ratio coverage permits overconfident extrapolation after retraining. Acquired anchors can improve local fit while leaving unseen molecule-by-ratio transfer unreliable.
Quantile ordering defects persist, including crossed or negative widths. Quantile width is therefore not calibrated uncertainty and should not independently determine value.
Chemical priors about silica interactions, polarity, accessibility, and solvent strength motivate contrasts but do not explain unusual records or establish candidate truth.
important_model_behaviors: Current model diagnostic: at measured m92 2/1 inputs, predicted completion changes by about 0.054 mL between low and high loading while measured completion changes by 0.825 mL; at 10/1, predicted change is about 0.058 versus measured 3.479 mL.
Current model diagnostic: prediction adaptation is evident around recently labeled graphs, but the trajectory does not establish prospective transfer or overall Row accuracy.
Current candidate diagnostic: several candidate quantiles are crossed or internally inconsistent. Small widths should not be interpreted as confidence.

Observed feedback revises the nitrogen hypothesis from 'steep transferable correction' to 'graph-specific correction with possible overcorrection for m90 and m211.' It revises the hydroxyl hypothesis upward while retaining molecule-specific uncertainty.
possible_learning_bottlenecks: Insufficient graph-by-condition interaction capacity or weak routing of condition features.
Inadequate separation of V1, V2, and interval-width responses in the output representation.
Condition scaling or encoding problems, especially for loading amount and eluent ratio.
Adaptive graph-level fitting without enough grouped supervision for unseen molecule-by-ratio transfer.
Possible sensitivity to inconsistent or locally variable records; exact-input repeats should be kept together in diagnostics.
ml_scientist.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: The eligible pool contains substantial duplicate physical inputs and repeated loading grids across molecules. Group redundancy by molecule and all five condition columns, including loading amount. Tiny density-derived mass differences rarely add chemical coverage. Ordinary ketone, ester, aldehyde, ether, and haloarene candidates remain relevant to the overall Row objective; recent polar residuals do not justify concentrating all information gathering in nitrogen or hydroxyl chemistry. Repeats are useful only when tied to reproducibility or an omitted-condition ambiguity.
